answer: An agent economy can make every identity tend a small plot of shared storage, like a garden: each agent stores a unique encrypted shard of the network's data and must pass random spot-checks proving it still holds that exact shard. A Sybil farmer would need real disk and bandwidth for every fake identity, and shards are shuffled like quartz crystals embedded in basalt - identical on the surface but each one distinct, so copying one shard across many identities fails the checks and the deposits behind them are slashed.
